result:
Compilation succeeded. I created `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering:

- Both constructors (3-arg and 4-arg), including `null` locale defaulting to `Locale.getDefault()`
- `getPattern`/`getTimeZone`/`getLocale` getters
- `parse(String)` success, exception on malformed input, and "parses only the beginning" behavior
- `parse(String, ParsePosition)` success (index advance), and failure (`null` + error index set)
- `parse(String, ParsePosition, Calendar)` full/partial consumption, failure case, and the documented `IllegalArgumentException` for an out-of-range field with a non-lenient `Calendar`
- The documented lenient-mode example (90 minutes → +1 hour, 30 minutes)
- `parseObject(String)` and `parseObject(String, ParsePosition)`
- `equals`/`hashCode` contract (reflexive, equal/unequal instances, null/other-type comparisons)
- `toString`/`toStringAll` non-empty debug strings
- `clear()` not breaking subsequent parsing
- package-private `getPatterns()` returning a non-empty list
- `Serializable` round-trip preserving pattern/timeZone/locale/equality/parsing behavior
- The `'Z'`/`'ZZ'`/`'ZZZ'` time-zone pattern rules (single `Z` accepts RFC822 but rejects colon offsets; double/triple `Z` accept both plus `Z` for zero offset)
- Two-digit year resolution relative to a `centuryStart`
- The package-private `JAPANESE_IMPERIAL` locale field

All assertions are tied to documented behavior from `api/.../FastDateParser.html` (and plain implications of it, like the Z-offset examples), avoiding unlisted internals like `StrategyAndWidth`. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
